questions.question: The British East India Company captured Pondicherry (Puducherry) from the French in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1761**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The British East India Company **captured **Pondicherry (Puducherry)** from the French in the year **1761**.
 
• **Puducherry **changed hands throughout the **Anglo-French wars from 1742 to 1763,** with the British "East India Company" capturing Puducherry from the French in 1761 and the French Company administration being **restored by the Treaty of Paris in 1763.**
 
• **The British "East India Company" **acquired control of the territory during the French Revolution in 1793, and it was returned to the French "East India Company" in 1814.
 
• When the British "East India Company" took control of India in the late 1850s, the French "East India Company" was allowed to keep their settlements in Pondicherry, Mahe, Yanam, Karaikal, and Chandernagore.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The former French colonies of Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam** now make up the Union Territory of Puducherry.
 
• The states of Tamilnadu and Kerala surround the Puducherry and Karaikal regions, while Kerala surrounds Mahe, and Andra Pradesh surrounds Yanam.
 
• Pondicherry was founded in 1673 after the "La Compagnie française des Indes Orientales" was granted firman by the Qiladar of Valikondapurarm, who served under the Sultan of Bijapur.
 
• A French Company Official named Bellanger moved into the Danish Lodge at Pondicherry on February 4, 1673.

questions.question: Who among the following Rajput rulers defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithviraj Chauhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rajput ruler Prithviraj Chauhan **defeated **Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain **in** 1191 AD**.
 
• Near Tarain, in 1191, the invading Ghurid army led by Muhammad of Ghor and the Rajput confederacy led by Prithviraj Chauhan fought the First Battle of Tarain, also known as the **First Battle of Taroari **(modern Taraori in Haryana, India).
 
• The Rajputs won the battle decisively, but Shihabuddin managed to flee and return to Ghor.
 
• After the Ghorid armies were routed, they retreated to the Ghazni, leaving a garrison of 2,000 soldiers under Zia ud-Din Tulaki to secure the fort of Tabarhind and delay the Rajput army for thirteen months, during this time Shahabuddin raised a stronger army of 120,000 men and invaded again, leading to the **Second Battle of Tarain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Prithviraj III, also known as Prithviraj Chauhan, **was a monarch of the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty who controlled the Sapadalaksha region, with his capital in Ajmer, Rajasthan.
 
• He inherited an empire that stretched from Thanesar in the north to Jahazpur (Mewar) in the south, which he sought to expand through military campaigns against neighbouring kingdoms, particularly the Chandelas.
 
• Muhammad Ghori's initial raids were against Multan and the citadel of Uch in 1175, with the goal of reuniting the Muslim nations of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rao Maldeo Rathore **was a Marwar monarch from the Rathore family who controlled the kingdom of Marwar, which is now part of the state of Rajasthan.
 
• **Maharana Kumbha,** also known as Kumbhakarna Singh, was the Maharana of the Mewar kingdom in India.
 
• **Bappa Rawal **was the monarch of Rajasthan, India's Mewar kingdom.

questions.question: The allocation towards health and well-being was increased by ______ over the previous year in Union Budget 2021-22.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__137%__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The allocation towards health and well-being **was increased by **137% **over the previous year in **Union Budget 2021-22**. 
 
• According to analysts, one of the sectors that have continually been neglected is "health."
 
• However, in her Budget 2021-22, **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** announced a **137 percent increase** in the allocation for health from the previous year's budget estimate of over **Rs. 94,000 crore (Rs. 94,452 crore) **and a 118 percent increase from the previous year's revised budget of over Rs. 1.02 lakh crore (Rs. 1,02,873 crore).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 2.23 lakh crore spending in Budget 2021 **comprises allocations to the Ministry of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy, as well as the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), which is the country's focal ministry for healthcare (AYUSH).
 
• To calculate the spending for health and wellness, the Finance Minister combined the amounts given under several categories of other ministries.

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as the ‘White Mountain’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhaulagiri I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhaulagiri I** is also known as the** ‘White Mountain’.**
 
• Dhaulagiri, at 8,167 metres above sea level, is the **world's seventh-tallest mountain** and the highest mountain within a single country's borders (Nepal).
 
• A Swiss-Austrian-Nepali expedition climbed it for the first time on May 13, 1960.
 
• Dhaulagiri is 34 kilometres east of Annapurna I (8,091 metres).
 
• **The Kali Gandaki River **flows between them in the world's deepest gorge, the Kaligandaki Gorge.
 
• Pokhara is a major regional city and the gateway for climbers and trekkers exploring both ranges, as well as a tourist destination in its own right, located south of the Annapurnas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cho Oyu**, at 8,188 metres above sea level, is the world's sixth tallest peak.
 
• **Lhotse**, at 8,516 metres, is the world's fourth-highest peak, behind Mount Everest, K2, and Kangchenjunga.
 
• At 8,485 metres, **Makalu** is the world's fifth-highest peak. It is 19 kilometres southeast of Mount Everest in the Mahalangur Himalayas, on the boundary between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region.

questions.question: Pneumatophores are specialised _______ in hydrophytes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**roots**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Pneumatophores** are specialized **root structures** that grow out from the water surface and help hydrophytic plants, such as many **mangrove species, get the aeration they need for root respiration.**
 
• Pneumatophores are specialized roots that sprout vertically out of the water or mud to reach the air and get oxygen for the root systems of marshy or tidal trees.
 
• **Pneumatophores** include mangrove knees and bald cypress. It is also known as the air root.
 
• These unique aerial roots allow plants to breathe air in wet environments. The roots can grow up from the stem or down from traditional roots.
 
• If they emerge from the earth, some botanists define them as aerating roots rather than aerial roots.

 [IMAGE: https://cmds-test.vedantu.com/prod/question-sets/d0a5edbf-0169-4ae8-97d9-eb9f1a6a5fd91808362618790778281.png]

questions.question: Which of the following is an Indirect Tax in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Goods and Services Tax (GST**) is a tax on goods and services.
 
• It is an** indirect tax **that was implemented to replace a variety of other indirect taxes such as VAT, service tax, purchase tax, excise duty, and so on.
 
• GST is a tax applied in India on the supply of **certain goods and services**.
 
• GST is a multi-stage, all-encompassing tax system that applies to the sale of goods and services.
 
• The fundamental goal of this taxing scheme, which is applicable throughout India, is to reduce the cascading effect of other indirect taxes.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The tax **on the consumption of goods and services is known as indirect tax. It isn't based on a person's earnings. Instead, he or she must pay the tax in addition to the cost of the products or services purchased from the seller.
 
• **Corporation tax **is a direct tax levied on corporations' net revenue or profit.
 
• **An income tax** is a type of tax that is levied on individuals or businesses based on their earnings or profits.
 
• If most investments are kept for at least one year**, capital gains **taxes must be paid on the earnings from their sale.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Only marketed goods are considered while estimating Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

II. The work done by a woman at her home is outside the purview of Gross Domestic Product.

III. In estimating GDP, only final goods and services are considered.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The total monetary or market worth **of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a certain time period is known as **Gross Domestic Product(GDP)**. 
 
• GDP includes the total value of final products that are produced and sold (and not resold) within the current year.
 
• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a country's economic health because it is a wide measure of entire domestic production.
 
• 
 In a free market economy, GDP includes only those products that are sold through the market. That is, consumers are willing to pay prices for the products they consume. In principle, GDP does NOT include those products consumers do not pay for. ***Hence statement 1 is correct.***
 
 
• Non-monetary goods and services (e.g. cooking by a housewife) are not included in GDP calculation. *Hence statement 2 is correct.*
 
• To avoid double-counting (adding the value of output to the GDP more than once), GDP only counts the ultimate output of commodities and services, not intermediary items or labour value in the supply chain. *Hence statement 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GDP represents the monetary value of a country's** final goods and services—those that are purchased by the end-user—produced over a specific period of time (say a quarter or a year).
 
• It counts all of the products produced within a country's borders. GDP is made up of commodities and services generated for market sale as well as certain nonmarket production, such as government-provided defence and education services.
 
• Gross national product, or GNP, is an alternative definition that counts all of a country's residents' productivity.

questions.question: ______ was an important port city in ancient India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamralipti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamralipti** was an **ancient Bengal port city** and the **capital of the Suhma Kingdom,** located on the Bay of Bengal's shore.
 
• It is typically attributed to the Tamluk town in modern-day Purba Medinipur, West Bengal. It was close to the river Rupnarayan.
 
• Its name comes from the Sanskrit term "tmra," which refers to copper, which was mined nearby at Ghatsila in the Chota Nagpur Plateau's Singbhum region and traded through this port.
 
• Tamralipta was the principal emporium under the Gupta era, acting as a point of departure for trade with Ceylon, Java, and China, as well as the west.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ancient capital of Northern Panchala, a northern Indian kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata, was **Ahichchhatra**, located near the contemporary Ramnagar hamlet in Aonla tehsil, Bareilly district in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **Champa** was the capital of the Anga empire in ancient India (a region corresponding with the eastern part of present-day Bihar state).
 
• **Shravasti** was the capital of the Kosala kingdom in ancient India, and it was here that the Buddha spent the most of his time after enlightenment.

questions.question: With which of the following oceans would you associate the ‘Ring of Fire’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pacific**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Many volcanic eruptions and earthquakes** occur in the **Ring of Fire**, which runs along much of the **Pacific Ocean's rim**.
 
• **The Ring of Fire **is a 40,000 km long and up to 500 km broad horseshoe-shaped ring.
 
• **The Pacific coasts of South America, North America, and Kamchatka**, as well as certain islands in the western Pacific Ocean, make up the Ring of Fire.
 
• Although geologists agree on almost all of the locations that make up the Ring of Fire, the dispute on the inclusion or exclusion of a few areas, such as the Antarctic Peninsula and western Indonesia.
 
• Plate tectonics, specifically the movement, collision, and destruction of lithospheric plates beneath and around the Pacific Ocean, has created the Ring of Fire.
 
• There is no single geological feature that makes up the Ring of Fire. Each segment of the Ring of Fire experiences volcanic eruptions and earthquakes independently of eruptions and earthquakes in other parts of the Ring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Pacific Ocean** is the world's largest and deepest oceanic division.
 
• It stretches from the Arctic Ocean to the Southern Ocean in the south and is bordered on the west by Asia and Australia, and on the east by the Americas.
 
• With a surface area of 70,560,000 km², **the Indian Ocean** is the third largest of the world's five oceanic divisions. Asia to the north, Africa to the west, and Australia to the east define its borders.
 
• **The Atlantic Ocean** is the world's second-largest ocean, covering approximately 106,460,000 km².
 
• Of the world's five major oceans, **the Arctic Ocean **is the smallest and shallowest. It is the coldest of all the seas, covering an area of approximately 14,060,000 km².

questions.question: Who among the following became the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand in March 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tirath Singh Rawa**____**t**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tirath Singh Rawat **became the **Chief Minister of Uttarakhand in March 2021**. 
 
• He is a former Chief Minister of Uttarakhand and a serving Member of Parliament in India.
 
• In the 2019 Indian general election, he was elected to the 17th Lok Sabha from the Garhwal constituency as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
 
• From 9 February 2013 until 31 December 2015, he was the party head of the Bharatiya Janata Party Uttarakhand and a former member of the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly from the Chaubattakhal constituency from 2012 to 2017.
 
• He was also** Uttarakhand's first Education Minister**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Madan Kaushik** is the state president of the BJP in Uttarakhand and a four-time MLA from Haridwar.
 
• **Dhan Singh Rawat** is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Cabinet Minister of Uttarakhand.
 
• From 2007 to 2009, and again from 2011 to 2012, Indian politician **Major General Bhuwan Chandra Khanduri** served as Chief Minister of Uttarakhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The chief minister of Uttarakhand **is the state's chief executive.
 
• The governor is a state's de jure head, while the chief minister has de facto executive authority, according to the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In which of the following states/union territories was an election NOT held during March-April 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The election was NOT held in Bihar during ****March**-**April 2021**.
 
• **Members of the Seventeenth Bihar Legislative Assembly** were elected in three parts from October to November.
 
• The previous Bihar Sixteenth Legislative Assembly's tenure concluded on November 29, 2020.
 
• Following the elections, incumbent Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was re-sworn in as Chief Minister after being chosen as the leader of the National Democratic Alliance in Bihar, and two new deputy Chief Ministers, Tarkishore Prasad, and Renu Devi were recruited into the new administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The election for 292 of the 294 constituencies of **West Bengal's Legislative Assembly in 2021** was held in eight phases between March 27 and April 29, 2021.
 
• The election for the remaining two seats had been postponed until September 30, 2021.
 
• Despite opinion surveys generally expecting a close fight against the Bharatiya Janata Party, which formed the formal opposition with 77 seats, the incumbent All India Trinamool Congress administration led by Mamata Banerjee won the election by a substantial margin.
 
• **On April 6, 2021, the Sixteenth Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Election **was conducted to elect representatives from the state's 234 constituencies. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) won the election, ending the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam's decade-long reign (AIADMK).
 
• M. K. Stalin, the leader of the DMK, was elected as the eighth Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, and the 12th since the 1956 reorganization. He took the place of AIADMK leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami.
 
• **The fifteenth legislative assembly election **was held on April 6, 2021, in the union territory of **Puducherry,** India, to elect members to the Legislative Assembly from 30 constituencies.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Secret of the Veda’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Aurobindo.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book **‘The Secret of the Veda' **was written by **Sri Aurobindo.**
 
• This volume comprises Sri Aurobindo’s writings on and translations of the **Rig Veda** that were published in the monthly review '**Arya**' between **1914 **and **1920**.
 
• Most of this material appeared under three headings:
 
 
• **The Secret of the Veda**, August 1914 – July 1916.
 
• **Selected Hymns**, August 1914 – July 1915.
 
• **Hymns of the Atris**, August 1915 – December 1917.
 
 
 
• **Sri Aurobindo **was an Indian nationalist and freedom fighter, a major Indian English poet, philosopher, and yogi.
 
• He joined the movement for India's freedom from British rule and for a duration (1905–10), became one of its most important leaders, before turning to develop his own vision and philosophy of human progress and spiritual evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda**, born **Narendranath Datta**, was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, and author. He was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna.
 
• **Annie Besant** was a British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, orator, political party member, educationist, and philanthropist. Regarded as a champion of human freedom, she was an ardent supporter of both Irish and Indian self-rule. In 1916 she established the Indian Home Rule League, of which she became president. She became the **first woman President of the Indian National Congress **to head the **Calcutta **session of the Indian National Congress in **1917**. 
 
• **Jiddu Krishnamurti **was a philosopher, speaker, and writer. In his early life, he was groomed to be the new World Teacher, an advanced spiritual position in the theosophical tradition, but later rejected this mantle and withdrew from the organization behind it. He was the adopted son of **Annie Besant.**

questions.question: Which of the following teams won the Indian Super League 2020-21?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• Mumbai City FC became the second Indian team to qualify for the AFC Champions League group stages. Mumbai City Football Team is an Indian professional football club based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, that participates in India's top flight, the Indian Super League.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **NorthEast United FC** is an Indian professional football team headquartered in Guwahati, Assam, that participates in India's top division, the Indian Super League. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The theme for International Mother Earth Day, 2021 was ‘________’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Restore our Earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The theme for International Mother Earth Day, 2021** was **'Restore our Earth'.**
 
• Every year on** April 22nd,** the world celebrates Earth Day, also known as **International Mother Earth Day.**
 
• **The Earth Day 2022 Theme is Invest In Our Planet.**
 
• The day will be commemorated around the world to raise awareness about the environment and encourage people to support environmental protection.
 
• **The 51st anniversary **of World Earth Day, which began in 1970, celebrated in 2021.
 
• In 2009, the United Nations renamed Earth Day International Mother Earth Day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Earth Day** was established in** 1970 **when around 20 million Americans felt that maintaining Mother Earth was a critical need.
 
• As a result, Earth Day was observed for the first time this year.
 
• Every year, billions of people throughout the world participate in various activities such as tree planting, cleanliness campaigns, and other activities to help Mother Nature.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India added a new fundamental duty under Article 51-A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002** added a new fundamental duty** under Article 51-A**.
 
• The Constitution of India's Eighty-sixth Amendment guarantees the right to education for children aged six to fourteen and early childhood care for children under the age of six.
 
• It has replaced Article 45 (Early Childhood Education) of directive principles of State policy with Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right) and altered **Article 51A (Fundamental Duties)** to establish a new duty of parents to provide education to their children aged six to fourteen years.
 
• In part III of the constitution, the 86th Amendment Act of 2002 established the right to education as a fundamental right. "Who is a parent or guardian to provide chances for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the ages of six and fourteen years," was added after clause (J).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Constitution (88th Amendment) Act, 2003: **The Union and States collect and appropriate service taxes, which are levied by the Union. Articles 268, 270, and the VIIth Schedule are amended by the Act.
 
• The main goal of the** 85th Amendment Act of 2001 **was to extend the advantage of the reservation to SC/STs in areas of promotion and subsequent seniority.

questions.question: At least ________ of the carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by algae through photosynthesis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a half**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Algae photosynthesis** accounts for **at least half of all carbon dioxide fixing** on the planet.
 
• They enhance the amount of dissolved oxygen in their immediate environment because they are **photosynthetic**.
 
• The conversion of inorganic carbon to organic carbon by living organisms is known as carbon dioxide fixation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biological carbon fixation, **also known as** carbon assimilation,** is the process by which living organisms transform inorganic carbon (most commonly in the form of carbon dioxide) into organic compounds.
 
• After that, the compounds are employed to store energy and provide structure for other biomolecules.
 
• Carbon is typically fixed through photosynthesis, however, in the absence of sunshine, some organisms use a process called chemosynthesis.
 
• **Photosynthesis **is the process through which plants produce oxygen and energy in the form of sugar from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
 
• **Plants, algae, and some bacteria **are involved in the process, which gathers energy from the sun to produce oxygen (O2) and chemical energy stored in glucose (a sugar). Herbivores get their energy from plants, while predators get theirs from herbivores.

questions.question: Which of the following days is celebrated as ‘World Water Day’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22 March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **World Water Day** is an** annual United Nations (UN)** commemoration held on **March 22 **that emphasises **the importance of clean water.**
 
• The day is used to advocate for sustainable freshwater resource management.
 
• Each day's subject focuses on topics related to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH), which aligns with the Sustainable Development Goal 6 aims.
 
• **World Water Day** is organized by **UN-Water**, which chooses the theme each year in conjunction with UN institutions with a stake in the topic.
 
• The subject for 2021 was** "Valuing Water," **and the public campaign encouraged individuals to "give us their tales, opinions, and feelings about water" in a worldwide debate on social media. 
 
• World Water Day is observed with a variety of activities all across the world.
 
• The day could also feature fundraising initiatives for water projects. In 1993, the United Nations declared the inaugural World Water Day.

questions.question: In which year was the ‘Lotteries Regulation Act’ passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1998**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lotteries Regulation Act of 1998** is a significant piece of law that establishes detailed standards for **the central government's handling of Indian lotteries.**
 
• It also permits state governments to conduct and regulate lotteries under certain conditions.
 
• This legislation was passed on the 7th of July, 1998, and went into effect on the 2nd of October, 1998. The Lotteries (Regulation) Ordinance of 1998 is repealed.
 
• Furthermore, the phrase "bumper draw of the lottery" is defined in **Section 2 (a) of the Act **as a special lottery drawn on any festival or a special occasion where the offered prize money is greater than the prize money offered in a regular draw of lotteries.
 
• **According to Section 2 (b)** of the Lotteries Regulation Act, a lottery is "a programme in which prizes are distributed by choosing the fate of ticket purchasers by lot or chance."​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lotteries **have long been a popular kind of gambling around the world.
 
• They were typically sold during the medieval period to collect funds for the town's defences and to assist the area's poor.
 
• While many Indian gambling laws apply to all forms of gambling in India**, the Lotteries Regulation Act of 1998** is separate legislation that governs the Indian lottery system.
 
• The legislation was written with the intention of regulating the buying and selling of lotteries in the country and, as a result, bringing the entire lottery selling industry under the control of the government.

questions.question: According to Ramsar Convention, which of the following is World Wetlands Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd**____** February**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Wetlands Day** is an** environmental celebration **that began in 1971 when a group of environmentalists gathered to reaffirm the protection and love for wetlands, which are small ecosystems of plant life and organisms found within water bodies that provide abundant ecological health to not only water bodies but entire environments.
 
• The World Wetlands Secretary Department is based in** Gland, Switzerland**, and according to the Ramsar Convention, the first acknowledgment of World Wetlands Day was given to "the Iranian city of Ramsar on the Caspian Sea's banks."
 
• Every year on the second of February, **World Wetlands Day **is commemorated, but it was not established until **1997**.
 
• This day honours the good impact that wetlands have had on the world, as well as the importance of bringing people together for the benefit of Mother Nature.
 
• This day also increases global awareness about the importance of wetlands to people and the environment.
 
• On this day, community guardians and environmentalists join together to celebrate their love for nature via a festival that recognizes what wetlands have done for not only humans but all living things.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ramsar Convention **on Internationally Significant Wetlands Waterfowl Habitat is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, which is particularly important.
 
• It's also known as the Wetlands Convention. It takes its name from the Iranian city of Ramsar, where the treaty was signed in **1971**.
 
• Representatives of the contracting parties gather every three years at the Conference of the Contracting Parties (COP), the convention's policy-making organ, to adopt decisions (resolutions and recommendations) to administer the convention's activities and strengthen the parties' ability to achieve its goals.

questions.question: On which day was the National Emblem of India adopted?
questions.solution:

• **The National Emblem of India **was adopted on** 26th January 1950**.
 
• It is a representational seal of the Republic of India, based on **Ashoka Pillar's Lion Capital **(based in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh.)
 
• The Indian National Emblem's motto is** 'Satyamev Jayate,**' which means** 'Truth Alone Triumphs.'**
 
• The National Emblem is a symbol of power that appears in all official government communications.
 
• "A heraldic instrument or symbolic object as a unique insignia of a nation, organization, or family," according to the definition.
 
• A nation's National Emblem is a seal that is used for official purposes and commands the highest respect and allegiance. 
 
• The National Emblem of India may only be used in accordance with the provisions of the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act-2005, and any unauthorized use is illegal.

questions.question: ________ is reducing the degree or intensity of, or eliminating, pollution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abatement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abatement **is reducing the degree or intensity of or eliminating, pollution.
 
• **Restoration, reclamation, or recovery of natural resources **are examples of abatement methods for reducing the degree or intensity of pollution.
 
• Only until the causes of pollution have been thoroughly identified can pollution abatement strategies be successfully implemented.
 
• Because it is intimately linked to urban planning, urban greenery and its role in pollution abatement is an interesting and emerging topic that demands joint work from specialists from other fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aeration **is the circulation of air through, mixing with, or dissolving in a liquid or other fluid-like substance.
 
• In air or another gas, an **aerosol** is a suspension of small solid particles or liquid droplets. Natural or anthropogenic aerosols can exist.
 
• **Absorption** is a physical or chemical phenomenon in which atoms, molecules, or ions enter a bulk phase, such as a liquid or solid material.
